subject: ss-rheumatology-immunology
title: Innate and adaptive immunity in rheumatic disease

steps.tx: Sensors of innate immunity identify danger signals through pattern recognition receptors. Surface **Toll-like receptor 4** or TLR4 recognises bacterial endotoxin and host endogenous alarmins such as HMGB1. Endosomal sensors **TLR7** and **TLR9** detect microbial and self nucleic acids including single-stranded RNA and unmethylated CpG DNA. Engagement of endosomal TLR pathways stimulates rapid **type I interferon** production, driving autoimmune pathogenesis in systemic lupus erythematosus.
steps.say: Pattern recognition receptors identify microbial and danger signals. Surface TLR4 identifies bacterial endotoxin and host alarmins. Endosomal TLR7 and TLR9 stimulate type one interferon production in systemic lupus.

vis.alt: Innate immune pattern recognition and complement activation pathways
vis.caption: Innate immune receptors and complement activation pathways in rheumatic autoimmunity. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.tx: Inflammatory caspases regulate acute crystal-mediated joint attacks through the **NLRP3 inflammasome**. Cytosolic assembly unites sensor NLRP3, adapter protein ASC, and **procaspase-1**. Autoproteolytic cleavage generates active enzyme **caspase-1**, which cleaves precursor peptides into mature secretable **IL-1beta** and **IL-18**. Uncontrolled inflammasome activation triggers intense neutrophil influx during acute flares of gout, pseudogout, and cryopyrin-associated periodic syndromes.
steps.say: The NLRP3 inflammasome regulates acute crystal inflammation. Sensor assembly generates active caspase-1 to cleave precursor peptides into interleukin-1 beta and interleukin-18. This pathway stimulates intense inflammation during acute flares.

nodes.label: Sensor NLRP3 and ASC bind procaspase-1

steps.tx: Lineage-determining cytokines guide naive CD4 positive T cell differentiation into functional helper subsets. Interleukin-12 and interferon-gamma direct **Th1** commitment via master regulator **T-bet**. Interleukin-4 promotes **Th2** differentiation through **GATA3**. Transforming growth factor-beta and interleukin-6 induce **Th17** differentiation through transcription factor **ROR-gamma-t**. Effector cytokines **IL-17A**, **IL-17F**, and **IL-22** stimulate tissue fibroblasts and recruit neutrophils in spondyloarthritis.
steps.say: Lineage cytokines direct naive helper T cell commitment. Interleukin-12 guides Th1 development, while interleukin-6 and TGF-beta induce Th17 cells through ROR-gamma-t. Th17 cytokines recruit neutrophils in spondyloarthritis.

steps.tx: Peripheral self-tolerance relies on **regulatory T cells** that express surface CD4, CD25, and nuclear master factor **FOXP3**. Inactivating mutations of the FOXP3 gene cause fatal systemic **IPEX syndrome**, characterised by immune dysregulation, polyendocrinopathy, enteropathy, and X-linked inheritance. Circulating regulatory T cells suppress self-reactive effector lymphocytes through inhibitory cytokines **IL-10** and **TGF-beta**, alongside contact-dependent co-inhibitory receptor **CTLA-4** signaling.
steps.say: Regulatory T cells express CD4, CD25, and nuclear factor FOXP3. Genetic deficiency of FOXP3 causes the fatal IPEX syndrome. Regulatory T cells suppress autoreactive lymphocytes through IL-10, TGF-beta, and CTLA-4.

steps.tx: Central B cell tolerance eliminates self-reactive immature lymphocytes within bone marrow. High-avidity engagement with self-antigen triggers **clonal deletion** or light chain **receptor editing**. Developing lymphocytes escaping into secondary lymphoid organs undergo **clonal anergy** or suppression by regulatory B cells. Autoreactive B cell longevity depends heavily on cytokine **BAFF**, whose pathological excess sustains autoantibody-producing clones in systemic lupus erythematosus.
steps.say: Central tolerance in bone marrow removes self-reactive immature B cells by clonal deletion or receptor editing. Excess BAFF promotes peripheral autoreactive B cell survival in lupus.

steps.tx: Proinflammatory cytokines orchestrate progressive articular erosion and destructive changes. Synovial macrophage-derived **TNF-alpha** and **IL-6** stimulate osteoclast differentiation by inducing mesenchymal **RANKL** expression. Concurrently, interleukin-23 promotes clonal survival of pathogenic Th17 cells. The resulting **IL-23/IL-17 axis** establishes persistent enthesitis, cartilage breakdown, and pathological new bone formation across axial and peripheral spondyloarthropathies.
steps.say: Tumor necrosis factor and interleukin-6 induce RANKL to drive osteoclast bone erosion. The interleukin-23 and interleukin-17 axis mediates enthesitis and new bone formation in spondyloarthritis.

steps.tx: Major histocompatibility complex polymorphisms convey major disease susceptibility in clinical rheumatology. The class I allele **HLA-B27** confers a relative risk exceeding **40** for ankylosing spondylitis through peptide presentation, heavy-chain homodimers, or endoplasmic reticulum stress. Conversely, the **shared epitope** encodes conserved pentapeptides **QKRAA** or **QRRAA** in **HLA-DRB1**, strongly predisposing to anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody-positive rheumatoid arthritis.
steps.say: Major histocompatibility alleles confer strong disease susceptibility. HLA-B27 raises the relative risk of ankylosing spondylitis above 40. The HLA-DRB1 shared epitope strongly predisposes to anti-CCP positive rheumatoid arthritis.

steps.tx: Autoimmune tissue injury frequently arises through **molecular mimicry** when pathogen antigens share structural homology with host self-peptides. In acute rheumatic fever, group A streptococcal **M protein** evokes cross-reactive antibody and cellular responses against cardiac **myosin** and basal ganglia. This structural mimicry produces carditis, Sydenham chorea, subcutaneous nodules, and migratory polyarthritis following untreated streptococcal pharyngitis.
steps.say: Molecular mimicry occurs when microbial antigens share structure with host proteins. Group A streptococcal M protein evokes cross-reactive immunity targeting cardiac myosin in acute rheumatic fever.
